draft.emotion: sincere and polite, with a warm nod of appreciation
notes: To sound polite, men usually add ครับ (khráp) and women add ค่ะ (khâ) at the end: ขอบคุณครับ / ขอบคุณค่ะ.
For deeper gratitude or when addressing elders and superiors, ขอบพระคุณ (khɔ̀ɔp-phrá-khun) is used; among close friends or to younger people, the casual ขอบใจ (khɔ̀ɔp-jai) is common.

senses.definition: Polite expression used to show gratitude.

examples.text: ขอบคุณสำหรับของขวัญค่ะ
ฉันอยากขอบคุณเขาที่ช่วยฉัน
examples.translation: I want to thank him for helping me.

draftBefore.emotion: sincere and polite, with a warm nod of appreciation
notes: In Thai, adding a polite particle at the end makes this expression even more gracious. Men typically add 'khrap' (ขอบคุณครับ) and women typically add 'kha' (ขอบคุณค่ะ).
Unlike in some languages, you do not need to repeat this word constantly. Using it once when someone does something specific is usually sufficient.

senses.definition: Words said to show you are grateful for something someone has done or given to you.

faults.why: Also commonly used as a transitive verb ('to thank someone'), which learners regularly encounter.
